newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Soccer-Dynamo Gazovik seek help from Russian gas company.
newsitem.headline: Soccer-Dynamo Gazovik seek help from Russian gas company.

text.p: Newly promoted Dynamo Gazovik said on Thursday they were looking to Russian gas monopoly Gazprom, the world's largest supplier of natural gas, for financial help as they prepare for the new premier league season.

Alexander Kolosov, president of the club from the gas-producing region of Tyumen in western Siberia, told Reuters that Gazprom were already helping install underground heating to enable them to play matches at home during cold weather.

But he said the club were hoping Gazprom and the Professional Football League (PFL) would provide more help with building a new stadium and other soccer facilities to meet the demands of playing at the top level in Russia.
"Negotiations are under way (with Gazprom)," Kolosov told Reuters by telephone, adding that the local Tyumen governor had been involved in the discussions on Dynamo's behalf.
"We hope Gazprom...will take us under their wing."
Dynamo won the first division title last season but already have problems before the new seasons kicks off in mid-March.

They are playing their first three games away because the underground heating is not ready, but hope the weather will warm up enough to allow them to play their April 5 fixture with premier league champions Spartak Moscow at home.
